series_key: swing extremes and pullbacks in mql5
mechanism: On HTF and LTF independently, detect N-bar swing highs/lows; keep last and previous of each. Classify STRUCT_BULLISH only if lastHigh>prevHigh AND lastLow>prevLow (HH+HL); STRUCT_BEARISH if lastLow<prevLow AND lastHigh<prevHigh (LL+LH); else STRUCT_NEUTRAL. HTF state is bias; LTF state is local structure.
data_needed: OHLC CopyRates on HTF and LTF (~100 bars); SwingBars lookback; SwingPoint last/prev high and low per TF.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Default HTF=H1, LTF=M5; SwingBars=3; chart-window indicator; any MT5 symbol
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an explicit dual-TF swing-structure regime tag (bullish/bearish/neutral) from consecutive swing comparisons rather than MA slope or single-break labels.
quote: if the latest high is greater than the previous high and the latest low is greater than the previous low, the market is classified as bullish (higher highs and higher lows). Conversely, if the latest low is lower than the previous low and the latest high is lower than the previous high, the structure is considered bearish

series_key: swing extremes and pullbacks in mql5
mechanism: Sell extreme when HTF bias is bearish AND bid > ltf_lastHigh + ATR(LTF)*ATR_Multiplier while also above ltf_lastLow. Buy extreme when HTF bias is bullish AND ask < ltf_lastLow - ATR*ATR_Multiplier. Overextension is volatility-normalized distance beyond the structural boundary, not a raw point break.
data_needed: iATR on LTF (period 14); ATR_Multiplier (default 1.0); LTF last swing high/low; HTF STRUCTURE_STATE; current bid/ask.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: HTF H1 bias + LTF M5 swings; ATR_Period=14; ATR_Multiplier=1.0
why_new_for_mis: Turns LTF swing breaks into a vol-adjusted extreme sensor—MIS can tag exhaustion only when price clears structure by a live ATR multiple, filtering noise breaches.
quote: A sell condition is only considered when the higher-timeframe bias is bearish, and price extends beyond the most recent LTF swing high by more than the defined ATR multiplier … signaling a volatility-adjusted extreme rather than a minor breakout.

series_key: swing extremes and pullbacks in mql5
mechanism: On each new LTF bar, if structure is bullish and close < ltf_lastLow, or structure is bearish and close > ltf_lastHigh, wipe all LTF swing memory and set STRUCT_NEUTRAL (also clear trade-swing stamps). Structure invalidation is an explicit regime-change event that forces rebuild from fresh swings.
data_needed: Latest LTF MqlRates close; ltfStructure; ltf_lastHigh/Low; ResetLTFStructure path.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: LTF default M5; evaluated on new LTF bar only
why_new_for_mis: MIS can emit a discrete structure-invalidation change flag when a close pierces the active swing extreme, separating failed regimes from ongoing HH/HL or LL/LH states.
quote: If a bullish structure is invalidated by price closing below the last swing low, or a bearish structure is broken by price closing above the last swing high, the existing structure is considered failed.

series_key: swing extremes and pullbacks in mql5
mechanism: Extreme bullish displacement: current bid above BOTH LTF lastHigh and lastLow (price has left the entire recent LTF range overhead). Extreme bearish: ask below lastLow. Interpreted as exhaustion/overextension for mean-reversion toward prior structure (TP inherits opposite swing), not as breakout continuation.
data_needed: LTF lastHigh and lastLow prices; current bid/ask; one-trade-per-swing time/price stamps.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: HTF H1 / LTF M5 EA; backtest H1 window 01 Dec 2025–01 Jan 2026
why_new_for_mis: Senses overextension as clearing the whole LTF swing envelope (above both bounds), a stronger displacement tag than a single swing break for MIS change/exhaustion events.
quote: When price aggressively trades below the LTF’s last low … both LTF_LastHigh and LTF_LastLow are positioned above the current market price—confirming structural displacement beneath the recent range. … During an extreme bullish move … both LTF_LastHigh and LTF_LastLow are now below the current market price.

series_key: swing extremes and pullbacks in mql5
mechanism: Raw N-bar swing highs/lows are candidates only. Promote to valid if ANY of: (A) Break of Structure vs prior valid extreme, (B) Displacement—candle range > avgCandleSize*DisplacementFactor, (C) Liquidity sweep—wick beyond prior swing then close back inside, (D) Time-based respect—level unviolated for StructureHoldBars. Invalid candidates stay noise.
data_needed: SwingLookback; avg candle range over ~50 bars; DisplacementFactor (1.5); StructureHoldBars (3); validSwings history.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H1 backtest 01 Dec 2025–30 Jan 2026; PERIOD_CURRENT swings; ATR_Period=14 for context
why_new_for_mis: Filters swing points into a validity sensor (BoS/displacement/sweep/hold) so MIS can weight only institutionally meaningful structure nodes, not every local extreme.
quote: A swing is valid only if it shows a momentum-based Break of Structure (BoS), displacement via impulse candles, or results directly from a liquidity sweep. … Only swings that demonstrate Break of Structure, Displacement, Liquidity Sweep, or Time-Based Respect become valid.

series_key: swing extremes and pullbacks in mql5
mechanism: From valid swings, mark equal highs/lows when |price_i-price_j| < 10*_Point and same side (type=equal). Also mark unused valid swings as untouched pools. Each zone tracks taken=true once a bar high/low pierces it. Untaken zones are forward liquidity magnets.
data_needed: validSwings array; CopyRates ~100 bars; price tolerance 10 points; LiquidityZone{price,time,taken,isHigh,type}.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H1; equal-swing tolerance 10*_Point; chart rectangles for untaken zones
why_new_for_mis: Builds an explicit taken/untaken liquidity-pool map from equal and untouched validated swings—MIS can sense resting stop clusters and whether they have been consumed.
quote: This layer marks zones such as equal highs/lows and untouched swing points as liquidity pools, and tracks whether these zones have been taken.

series_key: swing extremes and pullbacks in mql5
mechanism: MarketState ∈ {ACCUMULATION, EXPANSION, DISTRIBUTION, REVERSAL}. Transitions use HH/HL bullishness and liquidity-sweep-failure: ACCUMULATION→EXPANSION if bullish; →DISTRIBUTION if not and enough swings; EXPANSION→DISTRIBUTION if not bullish else →REVERSAL on sweep failure; DISTRIBUTION↔ACCUMULATION/REVERSAL similarly. Entries gated to Expansion/Accumulation for buys and Distribution/Reversal for sells.
data_needed: validSwings (≥2); marketStruct.bullish from HH/HL; CheckLiquiditySweepFailure(); prior state.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H1; state label on chart; execution uses state as confluence gate
why_new_for_mis: Four-phase structural regime machine (not binary trend) driven by validated swings and sweep failures—MIS can tag accumulation vs expansion vs distribution vs reversal context.
quote: a Structural State Machine continuously evaluates the relationship between consecutive valid swings to determine the current market phase—Accumulation, Expansion, Distribution, or Reversal.

series_key: swing extremes and pullbacks in mql5
mechanism: For each untaken liquidity zone, if the latest bar wicks beyond the zone (high>zone for highs, low<zone for lows) but closes back inside, flag liquiditySweepFailed. That failure drives EXPANSION/DISTRIBUTION → REVERSAL in the state machine—rejection after stop-run as a regime-change precursor.
data_needed: liquidityZones with taken=false; latest ~10 MqlRates; close vs zone price.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H1; evaluated on new bar inside UpdateMarketState
why_new_for_mis: Treats failed liquidity grabs (sweep then close back) as an explicit reversal-change sensor feeding regime transitions—distinct from simple breakout or wick filters.
quote: when price attempts to take liquidity but fails to continue in that direction, often signaling a potential reversal. … price breaks above the zone and closes below it; for lows, the opposite applies.

series_key: swing extremes and pullbacks in mql5
mechanism: avgCandleSize = mean((high-low)/_Point) over recent bars. A swing candle is displacement-valid when its range > avgCandleSize * DisplacementFactor (default 1.5). Same factor gates entry confirmation candles (body size vs average). Measures impulse strength relative to local volatility baseline.
data_needed: ~50-bar OHLC ranges; DisplacementFactor; swing.candleSize; optional entry candle body in points.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: PERIOD_CURRENT; DisplacementFactor=1.5; used in ValidateSwings and buy/sell confirmation
why_new_for_mis: Local range-vs-average displacement sensor for impulse quality—MIS can flag structurally impulsive bars without relying solely on ATR or fixed point thresholds.
quote: CheckDisplacement() focuses on momentum, comparing the size of the swing’s originating candle to the average candle size to determine whether the move was impulsive rather than random.

mechanism: Maintain fast ATR(ATR_Period=14) and slow ATR(ATR_AvgPeriod=50). ratio = currentATR/avgATR → LOW_VOL if <0.7, NORMAL if <1.2, HIGH if <1.8, else EXTREME_VOL. Regime drives adaptive pullback depth caps and is logged on each trade.
data_needed: Two iATR handles on PERIOD_CURRENT; currentATR, avgATR; VolatilityRegime enum.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: PERIOD_CURRENT; ATR 14 vs ATR 50; backtest ~01 Apr 2026–30 May 2026
why_new_for_mis: Four-bucket vol regime from short/long ATR ratio is a clean MIS volatility-state tag that also modulates downstream pullback validity thresholds.
quote: The UpdateATRValues() function plays a key role in volatility adaptation by comparing the current ATR against a longer-term ATR average. This comparison classifies market conditions as low, normal, high, or extreme volatility.

mechanism: Retracement depth = distance from impulse end to next swing / impulse range. Base PullbackMinDepth=0.25, PullbackMaxDepth=0.65. Under LOW_VOL shrink max by 0.10; HIGH_VOL widen max +0.10 and ease min −0.05; EXTREME_VOL max +0.15, min −0.10. Same absolute pullback is healthy or dangerous depending on ATR regime.
data_needed: validSwings (≥3) paired into impulse legs; currentVolRegime; PullbackMinDepth/MaxDepth inputs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: PERIOD_CURRENT swing lookback 5; depth bounds 0.25–0.65 base
why_new_for_mis: Normalizes pullback acceptability to the live vol regime—MIS can score correction health as regime-conditional depth rather than fixed Fibonacci cutoffs.
quote: A 40-point pullback in a low-ATR environment is flagged as dangerously deep. The same 40 point during a high-ATR expansion phase is classified as healthy and tradable.

mechanism: ScorePullback 0–10: +4 if depth in adaptive [min,max], +2 if ATR-normalized depth in [0.8,2.0], +1.5 if candle overlap%>50, +1 if momentumDecaying (last counter body < 0.7×avg), +1.5 if compressionDetected; −3 if WEAK/INVALID. GetBestPullback picks highest score per direction; entries require score≥4.
data_needed: PullbackModel fields; MeasurePullbackEfficiency over ≤15 pullback bars; ScorePullback(adaptiveMin,adaptiveMax).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: PERIOD_CURRENT; quality gate score≥4 before buy/sell; HUD shows best bull/bear PB
why_new_for_mis: Composite pullback quality sensor (depth + ATR-norm + overlap + decay + compression) gives MIS a graded correction-health reading beyond binary pullback detection.
quote: ScorePullback() then assigns a score between 0 and 10 by combining retracement depth, ATR-normalized distance, pullback efficiency, momentum decay, volatility compression, and structural strength.

mechanism: DetectVolatilityCompression true when currentATR < avgATR * 0.8 during the pullback phase. Optional RequireCompression gate blocks entries without the coil. Interpreted as volatility contraction before expansion; score bonus +1.5 when present.
data_needed: currentATR vs avgATR; RequireCompression input; pullback.compressionDetected flag.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: ATR 14 vs ATR 50; RequireCompression default true
why_new_for_mis: Pullback-timed ATR compression (<80% of average) is a coil/expansion precursor sensor MIS can fuse with structure and liquidity tags.
quote: DetectVolatilityCompression() checks whether the current ATR has contracted below 80% of its longer-term average, which can indicate a period of reduced volatility before a potential expansion.

mechanism: Classify each impulse→retracement leg: PULLBACK_AGGRESSIVE depth<0.25; HEALTHY 0.25–0.50; DEEP 0.50–0.75; WEAK 0.75–1.00; INVALID >1.0 (structure failure). Parallel ATR-normalizedDepth = retracementDistance/currentATR. Regime labels feed scoring and visualization (30/50/70% zones).
data_needed: impulseStart/End, retracementPrice; retracementDepth; currentATR; PullbackRegime enum.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any PERIOD_CURRENT symbol in the EA; chart PB depth/regime/score labels
why_new_for_mis: Ordinal pullback-health regime (aggressive→invalid) plus ATR-normalized depth gives MIS a structured correction-state vocabulary tied to impulse legs.
quote: each pullback is classified into a regime that ranges from aggressive continuation to complete structural failure.

mechanism: SL = nearest validated swing beyond price ± atr*ATR_SL_Multiplier*0.3 buffer; fallback pure ATR*ATR_SL_Multiplier or fixed points. Trailing advances SL to newer intervening valid swings with the same ATR buffer so stop width breathes with volatility and structure.
data_needed: validSwings; currentATR; ATR_SL_Multiplier (1.5); position open/current price.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: PERIOD_CURRENT; ATR_SL_Multiplier=1.5; used in ExecuteTrade and ManageOpenPosition
why_new_for_mis: Combines validated structure anchors with ATR buffers into a live vol-adaptive risk-width sensor—MIS can report structure-aware stop distance by regime.
quote: Stop losses were decoupled from fixed points and anchored to ATR multiples. … The stop loss is calculated dynamically using both swing structure and ATR, ensuring it expands or contracts based on market conditions.
